name: Crashing Tank
description: The dwell all but full: the drive amplifier clips on every loud note and the tank crashes and splashes, as when an amplifier is kicked. For a dramatic hit, or to automate up for one bar.

name: Dub Spring
description: A long, dark tank held back 60 ms, all wet, for a return track: send a snare or a skank chord to it in bursts and let it boing.

name: Keys Spring
description: Three springs, wide and a little bright, at a moderate dwell: an electric piano or an organ in a room of coils.

name: Short Tank Slap
description: The short tank with two springs and a short decay: a tight, metallic bounce behind a snare or a percussive part.

name: Studio Spring Send
description: The long tank alone with the dwell at its middle, for a return track: the springs as a studio unit was used, clean unless a loud hit drives it.

name: Subtle Amp Spring
description: The short tank turned low behind a clean or crunchy amplifier, as most amplifiers' reverb knob is left: a little space and a little bounce, not heard as an effect.

name: Surf Drip
description: The long tank with three springs, the dwell well up and the tone bright: every picked note drips and a hard one crashes the springs. For surf and twang guitar, on the amplifier's clean channel.

name: Vocal Spring
description: Two springs, darker, held back 25 ms so the words come first: the boxy, bouncing reverb of 1960s records behind a voice.
